title: Pivoting and unpivoting (wide and long format)

videos.script: The commercial team keeps its targets in a spreadsheet. One row per shop, one column per month, and a total at the end. {{sheet}} That shape is perfect for reading. It is awkward for everything else. {{awkward}} To compare targets with sales, the months have to come down out of the header and become values in a column. That is called melting, or unpivoting. {{melt}} Do it carelessly, and the Total column melts too. It becomes a thirteenth month, and every shop's target for the year doubles. {{total}} Then the opposite move: sales recorded one per row, turned into a table with a column per month. That is pivoting. {{pivot}} Pivoting has its own trap. Two rows for the same shop and month must be combined somehow, and the tool either refuses or adds them up. {{dupes}} By the end, targets and sales sit side by side, one row per shop and month, and the question the team actually asked has an answer. {{end}}
